facts.raw_span: a 3-month history of rapidly spreading intensively pruritic papules on her extremities
no remarkable medical or family history
not concurrently being treated with any medications
scattered, erythematous, annular papules measuring up to 5 mm wide
a few asymptomatic brown flat papules scattered on her face
the palms, soles, and oral mucosa were not involved
Routine blood, liver and kidney function, antistreptolysin O, C-reactive protein, antinuclear antibody, and rheumatoid factor tests disclosed no abnormal findings
Mild hyperkeratosis accompanied by parakeratosis
Atrophy of the epidermis
Well-developed cornoid lamellae with a decreased granular layer
Individual cell dyskeratosis
Slight infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and eosinophils in the upper dermis

concepts.why: The patient's skin biopsy revealed mild hyperkeratosis, atrophy of the epidermis, and well-developed cornoid lamellae, which are characteristic of Grover's disease.
The patient's skin lesions and biopsy results, including hyperkeratosis and parakeratosis, are consistent with Darier's disease.
The patient's pruritic papules and erythematous lesions, along with the absence of systemic symptoms, are suggestive of Pityriasis rubra pilaris.
The patient's skin lesions, including scattered erythematous papules, are consistent with Psoriasis.
The patient's pruritic papules and absence of systemic symptoms are suggestive of Seborrheic dermatitis.
The patient's skin lesions, including erythematous papules, are consistent with Lichen planus.
The patient's skin biopsy revealed hyperkeratosis and parakeratosis, which are characteristic of Keratosis pilaris.
The patient's skin lesions and biopsy results, including hyperkeratosis and parakeratosis, are consistent with Ichthyosis vulgaris.
The presence of a slight infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and eosinophils in the upper dermis is consistent with the diagnosis of Mycosis fungoides.
